C-FIX-009-RECENTLY-CLOSED.IntentSummary: A single in-memory Pinia store owns the history; every UI surface (strip button + popover, welcome block, the reopen chord) is a thin consumer of its actions plus record/consume hooks at the two existing funnels: FORCE_CLOSE_TAB and the mt::open-new-tab arrival. No new persistence, no new backend surface except the menu item.

MustContain.Text: deduplicates a repeatedly closed pathname to its newest entry
Reopen all restores strip order and the active tab

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: store/recentlyClosed.js: entries newest-first bounded at 25; RECORD_CLOSE dedups by pathname to the newest close; CONSUME removes a matching entry; REOPEN_ONE stats first (missing drops the entry with a localized notice), opens through mt::open-file and consumes only on success; REOPEN_ALL reopens in ascending strip order, drops missing entries up front with one combined notice, and re-selects the was-active entry through the mt::recently-closed-select bus event; CLEAR empties; marker logs exist for verification.

T-002.Title: Record + consume hooks at the two funnels

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: FORCE_CLOSE_TAB records pathname tabs (strip index pre-splice, wasActive, workspace root) and never untitled tabs; the mt::open-new-tab arrival consumes the matching pathname so every open path stays honest.

tabs.vue renders the count-badged reopen button left of the + only while the history is non-empty; the popover teleports to body past the strip clip, anchors fixed under the button, shows header + Clear, rows (filename, root · relative time) and the Reopen-all footer, and closes on Escape/outside mousedown; a new chromeIcons 'reopen' glyph follows the frozen conventions.

recent/index.vue shows the block only at zero tabs with non-empty history: primary Reopen-closed-tab row with the platform chord hint, up to three older rows, Reopen-all chip when more than one entry remains; all actions delegate to the store.

T-005.Title: Chord, menu item and palette command

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: m009_menu.rs adds File › Reopen Closed Tab (Shift+CmdOrCtrl+T, id file.reopen-closed-tab) after Close Tab; commands/index.js maps the id to the mt::editor-reopen-closed-tab bus event; editor.js LISTEN_FOR_REOPEN_CLOSED reopens newest and handles the Reopen-all active selection; empty history is a quiet no-op allowlisted in the affordance audit.

recent.recentlyClosed.* (title, clear, reopenAll, reopenClosedTab, missingNotice, someMissingNotice, buttonLabel) and commands.file.reopenClosedTab exist in all ten source catalogs with exact minified derivatives; product names untranslated.

tests/e2e/recently-closed.spec.ts pins: close-all → Reopen all restores strip order + the was-active tab; single reopen with a missing file dropping to a notice; independent reopen consumes (no strip button left); the welcome primary action recovers the newest after the last close.
M-011 SummaryDelta, V-M-011 scenario-75 + commands, the train FIX-009 record and evidence.json reflect the implemented behavior; grace lint is clean.

C-1.Name: Close one saved tab, tabs remain
C-1.Expected: Entry recorded; strip button appears with count 1; popover lists it; the chord reopens and consumes; button disappears at empty.

C-2.Name: Close the same file repeatedly (open then close, three times)
C-2.Expected: History holds ONE entry (newest close); count never exceeds distinct live paths; the chord reopens once.

C-3.Name: Close all tabs to zero
C-3.Expected: Welcome shows the recovery block (primary reopen-newest + rows + Reopen all N); no "Last session" row appears from live state (the cold-start bundle owns that).

C-4.Name: Reopen all determinism
C-4.Expected: Files reopen in ascending strip order regardless of close order; the tab active at its close time ends active; dedup kept only newest metadata.

C-5.Name: Missing file on single reopen
C-5.Expected: Entry dropped; localized notice names the file; history count updates; other entries untouched.

C-6.Name: Missing files inside Reopen all
C-6.Expected: Existing files still reopen in order; one combined notice reports the missing count; missing entries dropped; active selection falls back to the newest available wasActive entry.

C-7.Name: Independent open consumes
C-7.Expected: Opening a history file via Recent files / dialog / drag / clipboard removes its entry (arrival funnel); count and welcome rows update reactively.

C-8.Name: Untitled tab closed
C-8.Expected: No entry (no pathname); button count unchanged; welcome never offers drafts.

C-9.Name: Workspace root removed
C-9.Expected: History unchanged (no hook on root removal); reopening a file whose root is gone still opens it as a loose tab.

C-10.Name: Bound overflow (30 closes)
C-10.Expected: 25 kept, oldest evicted; Reopen all still deterministic within the retained set.

C-11.Name: Cold relaunch after a closing run
C-11.Expected: History empty by construction (memory-only store); strip button absent; welcome shows only honest cold-start state.

C-12.Name: Chord key ownership
C-12.Expected: When history non-empty the chord reopens newest and never reaches muya; when empty it is a no-op; editor key handlers unaffected; Windows/Linux use Ctrl+Shift+T via CmdOrCtrl.

Correctness.Note: Single record funnel (FORCE_CLOSE_TAB) and single consume funnel (open-new-tab arrival) make double-recording and stale entries structurally impossible; reopen reuses mt::open-file so encoding/watcher/preview logic is not forked. Concern raised and resolved: consuming before the open resolves would lose the entry on a failed invoke — consume AFTER a successful invoke, and the arrival-funnel consume makes the popover path idempotent anyway. stripIndex captured pre-splice is the correct original position. Second defect found by the unit matrix and fixed: Reopen-all must consume missing entries too, or they linger in the list forever.

Security.Note: No new IPC commands; the popover renders pathname-derived filenames only (existing basename/shortenMiddle utils); notice messages embed a filename, same exposure class as existing toasts; no persistence, so nothing to leak across sessions.

UX.Note: Mockup-faithful popover (header/Clear, rows with root · time, Reopen-all footer); welcome block mirrors the mockup hierarchy; Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+T matches every browser convention; Escape/outside-click close; button hidden at zero so the strip stays clean; the count badge is the discoverability cue the owner asked for.

Performance.Note: Store ops are O(n) with n bounded at 25; Reopen-all stats in parallel then opens sequentially (same shape as RESTORE_SESSION, bounded by 25); popover renders only while open; no watchers beyond the two reactive gates.

Review.Findings: Pass A (correctness and GRACE contracts) and pass B (security, verification, UX) both returned APPROVE after verifying the wave-2 repairs with evidence (35/35 focused store/component tests, 27/27 Rust menu tests, ten-locale parity, publication-privacy 3/3, grace lint 0 errors): the frozen-payload restore and REOPEN_ALL accuracy implemented as specified with regressions. Minor findings fixed in the review commit: the cold-start spec/plan now name welcome.spec.ts (where the frozen-offer e2e lives) and declare the collateral test files; the RU terminology follows the established «сессия»; the selection comment states the rightmost-was-active mechanic; the duplicated describe header is gone; the m009 taxonomy carries file.reopen-closed-tab. The local-model review (qwen3:4b, 59 src+grace chunks across both PRs) produced one actionable finding — markers logged full paths; they now log basenames per the repo console-privacy convention — plus four dismissals with evidence: three chunk-boundary truncation artifacts (the m009 accelerator string, the tabs.vue relativeTime local wrapper, the homeDir import line — all complete in the real files) and the by-design missing-file drop (owner semantics, notice-pinned).
